headline: Revenue sets a record while one-time items swing EPS higher
summary_short: MGM Resorts posted record Q2 revenue of $4.45B (+1% y/y), with diluted EPS of $1.11 versus $0.18 a year ago, though Adjusted EPS fell to $0.59 from $0.79 as a large property-transactions gain and a $111M goodwill impairment moved in opposite directions.
summary_long: Consolidated revenue rose 1% y/y to a record $4.45B, with Las Vegas Strip Resorts up 3% for a second straight quarter of y/y growth and MGM Digital up 20%. Regional Operations revenue fell 4% y/y (same-store revenue rose 3%) after the April 2026 Northfield Park disposition; MGM China Segment Adjusted EBITDAR fell 15% y/y on a $21M rise in intercompany branding fees. GAAP diluted EPS jumped to $1.11 from $0.18, driven mainly by a large net property-transactions gain partly offset by a $111M goodwill impairment; Adjusted EPS, which excludes both, fell to $0.59 from $0.79. Cash rose to $2.55B and long-term debt fell to $6.07B; the company repurchased $164M of stock in the quarter. No numeric forward guidance was issued.

(2) The >100% and >500% q/q/y/y deltas on EPS, net income, and pretax income are mathematically correct but reflect a genuinely small prior-period base (e.g. diluted EPS of $0.18 a year ago) depressed by a $0.72/share FX transaction loss and a smaller property-transactions gain in that comparison quarter -- not a data error. (3) Net income's swing is driven almost entirely by two large, largely offsetting non-operating items disclosed in the release's own Adjusted-EPS reconciliation table: a net property-transactions gain (~+$1.13 EPS impact) and an $111M goodwill impairment (~-$0.37 EPS impact); readers should treat the y/y net-income comparison as one-time-item-driven, not a read on core operating momentum. drivers.explanation: CEO Bill Hornbuckle cited record consolidated revenue, a second straight quarter of Las Vegas Strip Resorts y/y growth, an all-time-best Regional Operations same-store quarter, and 20% y/y MGM Digital growth; CFO Jonathan Halkyard cited EBITDAR growth in Las Vegas and market-share gains at MGM China.

Las Vegas Strip Resorts revenue rose 3% y/y (second straight quarter of growth) and MGM Digital rose 20% y/y; Regional Operations revenue fell 4% y/y (same-store revenue rose 3%) after the April 2026 Northfield Park disposition, and MGM China was roughly flat.

The jump was driven mainly by a large net gain on property transactions (about +$1.13 to EPS per the company's own reconciliation), partly offset by a $111M goodwill impairment (about -$0.37 EPS); Adjusted EPS, which excludes both, fell y/y.
Net income growth was amplified by a 6.5% y/y drop in diluted share count as the buyback program ($164M repurchased this quarter) continued retiring shares.
Not explained in the release -- MGM's own release does not discuss 'gross profit' as a line item; this is a Yahoo-derived measure.
